sanskrit: śrīr uvāca sthāsyāmi nityaṃ devendra yathā tvayi nibodha tat vidhinā vedadṛṣṭena caturdhā vibhajasva mām
english: Śrī said: I shall abide with you forever, O lord of the gods, in the manner you desire. Mark this well: by the ordinance ordained in the Veda, divide me fourfold.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca ahaṃ vai tvā nidhāsyāmi yathāśakti yathābalam na tu me 'tikramaḥ syād vai sadā lakṣmi tavāntike
english: Śakra said: I shall indeed set you in place to the best of my power and strength; yet let there never be any overstepping by me, O Lakṣmī, while I remain near you.

sanskrit: bhūmir eva manuṣyeṣu dhāraṇī bhūtabhāvinī sā te pādaṃ titikṣeta samarthā hīti me matiḥ
english: Among men it is the Earth herself, the all-bearing, the mother of beings, who can endure your foot, for she is able—so I hold.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca eṣa me nihitaḥ pādo yo 'yaṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭhitaḥ dvitīyaṃ śakra pādaṃ me tasmāt sunihitaṃ kuru
english: Śrī said: Here is one foot of mine set down, this one that rests upon the Earth. Now, O Śakra, set my second foot firmly in its place.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca āpa eva manuṣyeṣu dravantyaḥ paricārikāḥ tās te pādaṃ titikṣantām alam āpas titikṣitum
english: Śakra said: It is the Waters among men, flowing and ministering to all, that shall endure your foot; the Waters are equal to enduring it.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca eṣa me nihitaḥ pādo yo 'yam apsu pratiṣṭhitaḥ tṛtīyaṃ śakra pādaṃ me tasmāt sunihitaṃ kuru
english: Śrī said: Here is one foot of mine set down, this one that rests upon the Waters. Now, O Śakra, set my third foot firmly in its place.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca yasmin devāś ca yajñāś ca yasmin vedāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ tṛtīyaṃ pādam agnis te sudhṛtaṃ dhārayiṣyati
english: Śakra said: He in whom the gods and the sacrifices, in whom the Vedas are established—Agni—shall bear your third foot, held firm and secure.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca eṣa me nihitaḥ pādo yo 'yam agnau pratiṣṭhitaḥ caturthaṃ śakra pādaṃ me tasmāt sunihitaṃ kuru
english: Śrī said: Here is one foot of mine set down, this one that rests upon the Fire. Now, O Śakra, set my fourth foot firmly in its place.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca ye vai santo manuṣyeṣu brahmaṇyāḥ satyavādinaḥ te te pādaṃ titikṣantām alaṃ santas titikṣitum
english: Śakra said: Those who among men are the good, devoted to brahman and speakers of truth—let them endure your foot; the good are equal to enduring it.

sanskrit: śrīr uvāca eṣa me nihitaḥ pādo yo 'yaṃ satsu pratiṣṭhitaḥ evaṃ vinihitāṃ śakra bhūteṣu paridhatsva mām
english: Śrī said: Here is one foot of mine set down, this one that rests upon the good. Thus deposited, O Śakra, dispose me among living beings.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca bhūtānām iha vai yas tvā mayā vinihitāṃ satīm upahanyāt sa me dviṣyāt tathā śṛṇvantu me vacaḥ
english: Śakra said: Whoever among living beings here should assail you, who have been duly set in place by me, that one shall be my enemy—so let them hear my word.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas tyaktaḥ śriyā rājā daityānāṃ balir abravīt yāvat purastāt pratapet tāvad vai dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Bali, the king of the Daityas, forsaken by Śrī, spoke thus: As far as the sun blazes in the east, so far also over the southern quarter,

sanskrit: paścimāṃ tāvad evāpi tathodīcīṃ divākaraḥ tathā madhyaṃdine sūryo astam eti yadā tadā punar devāsuraṃ yuddhaṃ bhāvi jetāsmi vas tadā
english: and so far too the maker of day shall blaze over the west and over the north; when at midday the Sun shall reach his setting—then once more shall come the war of gods and Asuras, and then I shall be your conqueror.

sanskrit: sarvāṃl lokān yadāditya ekasthas tāpayiṣyati tadā devāsure yuddhe jetāhaṃ tvāṃ śatakrato
english: When the Sun, standing in a single place, shall scorch all the worlds, then in the war of gods and Asuras I shall be your conqueror, O Śatakratu.

sanskrit: śakra uvāca brahmaṇāsmi samādiṣṭo na hantavyo bhavān iti tena te 'haṃ bale vajraṃ na vimuñcāmi mūrdhani
english: Śakra said: By Brahmā I have been instructed that you are not to be slain; therefore, O Bali, I do not loose my thunderbolt upon your head.

sanskrit: yatheṣṭaṃ gaccha daityendra svasti te 'stu mahāsura ādityo nāvatapitā kadā cin madhyataḥ sthitaḥ
english: Go where you will, O lord of the Daityas; may it be well with you, O great Asura. The Sun shall never scorch from a station fixed at the zenith.

sanskrit: sthāpito hy asya samayaḥ pūrvam eva svayaṃbhuvā ajasraṃ pariyāty eṣa satyenāvatapan prajāḥ
english: For his appointed course was ordained from of old by the Self-existent: ceaselessly he wheels about, warming the creatures with truth.

sanskrit: ayanaṃ tasya ṣaṇmāsā uttaraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ tathā yena saṃyāti lokeṣu śītoṣṇe visṛjan raviḥ
english: His course is of six months, the northern and likewise the southern, by which the Sun travels through the worlds, dispensing cold and heat.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktas tu daityendro balir indreṇa bhārata jagāma dakṣiṇām āśām udīcīṃ tu puraṃdaraḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by Indra, O Bhārata, Bali the lord of the Daityas went to the southern region, while Purandara went to the north.

sanskrit: ity etad balinā gītam anahaṃkārasaṃjñitam vākyaṃ śrutvā sahasrākṣaḥ kham evāruruhe tadā
english: Having heard this utterance sung by Bali, known as 'the discourse free of egotism,' the Thousand-eyed One then ascended into the sky.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam śatakratoś ca saṃvādaṃ namuceś ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: On this very theme they recount an ancient tale, the colloquy of Śatakratu and Namuci, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: śriyā vihīnam āsīnam akṣobhyam iva sāgaram bhavābhavajñaṃ bhūtānām ity uvāca puraṃdaraḥ
english: To Namuci, bereft of fortune yet seated unshaken like the ocean, knowing the rising and the passing of all beings, Purandara spoke thus:

sanskrit: baddhaḥ pāśaiś cyutaḥ sthānād dviṣatāṃ vaśam āgataḥ śriyā vihīno namuce śocasy āho na śocasi
english: Bound in fetters, fallen from your station, brought into the power of your foes, and stripped of fortune—O Namuci, do you grieve, or do you not grieve?

sanskrit: namucir uvāca anavāpyaṃ ca śokena śarīraṃ copatapyate amitrāś ca prahṛṣyanti nāsti śoke sahāyatā
english: Namuci said: Nothing is gained by grief, and the body is wasted by it, while one's enemies rejoice; there is no help in grieving.

sanskrit: tasmāc chakra na śocāmi sarvaṃ hy evedam antavat saṃtāpād bhraśyate rūpaṃ dharmaś caiva sureśvara
english: Therefore, O Śakra, I do not grieve, for all this is bounded by an end; through anguish both beauty and dharma fall away, O lord of the gods.

sanskrit: vinīya khalu tad duḥkham āgataṃ vaimanasyajam dhyātavyaṃ manasā hṛdyaṃ kalyāṇaṃ saṃvijānatā
english: Having truly subdued that sorrow born of dejection when it comes, the discerning one should turn his mind upon what is pleasing to the heart and wholesome.

sanskrit: yathā yathā hi puruṣaḥ kalyāṇe kurute manaḥ tadaivāsya prasīdanti sarvārthā nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: For in the very measure that a man sets his mind upon the good, in that measure do all his aims grow favorable—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: ekaḥ śāstā na dvitīyo 'sti śāstā; garbhe śayānaṃ puruṣaṃ śāsti śāstā tenānuśiṣṭaḥ pravaṇād ivodakaṃ; yathā niyukto 'smi tathā vahāmi
english: One alone is the Ruler; there is no second ruler. The Ruler governs the man lying yet in the womb. Directed by him, like water down a slope, even as I am appointed, so do I move along.

sanskrit: bhāvābhāvāv abhijānan garīyo; jānāmi śreyo na tu tat karomi āśāḥ suśarmyāḥ suhṛdāṃ sukurvan; yathā niyukto 'smi tathā vahāmi
english: Discerning well both being and non-being, I know the better course, yet I do not pursue it; fulfilling well the fond hopes of friends—even as I am appointed, so do I move along.

sanskrit: yathā yathāsya prāptavyaṃ prāpnoty eva tathā tathā bhavitavyaṃ yathā yac ca bhavaty eva tathā tathā
english: In whatever measure a thing is to be attained by him, in just that measure he attains it; and as whatever is to come to pass, so exactly does it come to pass.

sanskrit: yatra yatraiva saṃyuṅkte dhātā garbhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ tatra tatraiva vasati na yatra svayam icchati
english: Wherever the Ordainer joins the embryo, again and again, there alone does it dwell, and not where it itself would wish.

sanskrit: bhāvo yo 'yam anuprāpto bhavitavyam idaṃ mama iti yasya sadā bhāvo na sa muhyet kadā cana
english: He whose conviction is ever this—'This state that has befallen me was destined to be mine'—such a one is never bewildered.

sanskrit: paryāyair hanyamānānām abhiyoktā na vidyate duḥkham etat tu yad dveṣṭā kartāham iti manyate
english: For those struck down by the turns of fate there is found no real assailant; this alone is the suffering—that the hater thinks, 'I am the doer.'

sanskrit: ṛṣīṃś ca devāṃś ca mahāsurāṃś ca; traividyavṛddhāṃś ca vane munīṃś ca kān nāpado nopanamanti loke; parāvarajñās tu na saṃbhramanti
english: Upon whom in this world do calamities not press—the seers and the gods and the great Asuras, the elders learned in the threefold lore, and the sages in the forest? Yet those who know the higher and the lower are not thrown into confusion.

sanskrit: na paṇḍitaḥ krudhyati nāpi sajjate; na cāpi saṃsīdati na prahṛṣyati na cārthakṛcchravyasaneṣu śocati; sthitaḥ prakṛtyā himavān ivācalaḥ
english: The wise man neither rages nor clings, neither sinks into despair nor exults, nor grieves amid the straits and ruin of his fortunes; by his very nature he stands unmoved, like the Himālaya.

sanskrit: yam arthasiddhiḥ paramā na harṣayet; tathaiva kāle vyasanaṃ na mohayet sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca tathaiva madhyamaṃ; niṣevate yaḥ sa dhuraṃdharo naraḥ
english: He whom the highest success of his aims does not elate, and whom, when its hour comes, calamity does not bewilder, who meets pleasure and pain and the state between them all alike—that man is a true bearer of the yoke.

sanskrit: yāṃ yām avasthāṃ puruṣo 'dhigacchet; tasyāṃ rametāparitapyamānaḥ evaṃ pravṛddhaṃ praṇuden manojaṃ; saṃtāpam āyāsakaraṃ śarīrāt
english: Whatever condition a man may come into, in that let him find contentment, untormented; thus would he drive from his body the swelling anguish born of the mind, the bringer of toil.

sanskrit: tat sadaḥ sa pariṣatsabhāsadaḥ; prāpya yo na kurute sabhābhayam dharmatattvam avagāhya buddhimān; yo 'bhyupaiti sa pumān dhuraṃdharaḥ
english: That man of understanding who, having come into the assembly, the council, the company of its members, feels no dread of the assembly, who has plunged into the truth of dharma and stands by it—he is a bearer of the yoke.

sanskrit: prājñasya karmāṇi duranvayāni; na vai prājño muhyati mohakāle sthānāc cyutaś cen na mumoha gautamas; tāvat kṛcchrām āpadaṃ prāpya vṛddhaḥ
english: The deeds of the wise are hard to trace; surely the wise man is not bewildered in the hour of bewilderment. Even when fallen from his station, the aged Gautama was not bewildered, though he had met with such grievous calamity.

sanskrit: na mantrabalavīryeṇa prajñayā pauruṣeṇa vā alabhyaṃ labhate martyas tatra kā paridevanā
english: Not by the power and might of counsel, nor by wisdom, nor by manly effort, does a mortal gain what is not to be gained—so what cause for lament is there in that?

sanskrit: yad evam anujātasya dhātāro vidadhuḥ purā tad evānubhaviṣyāmi kiṃ me mṛtyuḥ kariṣyati
english: Whatever the Ordainers appointed of old for one born thus—that very thing shall I undergo; what can death do to me?

sanskrit: labdhavyāny eva labhate gantavyāny eva gacchati prāptavyāny eva prāpnoti duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca
english: What is to be obtained, that alone he obtains; where he is to go, there alone he goes; what is to be reached, that alone he reaches—both the sorrows and the joys.

sanskrit: etad viditvā kārtsnyena yo na muhyati mānavaḥ kuśalaḥ sukhaduḥkheṣu sa vai sarvadhaneśvaraḥ
english: That man who, knowing this in its fullness, is not bewildered, skilled amid pleasures and pains—he indeed is lord of all riches.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca magnasya vyasane kṛcchre kiṃ śreyaḥ puruṣasya hi bandhunāśe mahīpāla rājyanāśe 'pi vā punaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: For a man sunk in grievous calamity, in the loss of his kin, O guardian of the earth, or again in the loss of his kingdom—what is the better course?

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi naḥ paramo vaktā loke 'smin bharatarṣabha etad bhavantaṃ pṛcchāmi tan me vaktum ihārhasi
english: For you are our highest expounder in this world, O bull of the Bhāratas; this I ask of you, and you should declare it to me here.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca putradāraiḥ sukhaiś caiva viyuktasya dhanena ca magnasya vyasane kṛcchre dhṛtiḥ śreyaskarī nṛpa
english: Bhīṣma said: For one parted from sons and wife, from comforts and from wealth, sunk in grievous calamity, steadfastness is the better course, O king.

sanskrit: dhairyeṇa yuktasya sataḥ śarīraṃ na viśīryate ārogyāc ca śarīrasya sa punar vindate śriyam
english: For one who is endowed with firmness the body does not waste away, and through the body's soundness he wins back his fortune once more.

sanskrit: yasya rājño narās tāta sāttvikīṃ vṛttim āsthitāḥ tasya sthairyaṃ ca dhairyaṃ ca vyavasāyaś ca karmasu
english: That king, dear son, whose men hold to a sattvic way of conduct—his are stability and firmness and resolve in his undertakings.

sanskrit: atraivodāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam balivāsavasaṃvādaṃ punar eva yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this very theme they recount once more an ancient tale, the colloquy of Bali and Vāsava, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vṛtte devāsure yuddhe daityadānavasaṃkṣaye viṣṇukrānteṣu lokeṣu devarāje śatakratau
english: When the war of gods and Asuras was over, and the Daityas and Dānavas destroyed, when the worlds had been measured out by Viṣṇu's stride, and Śatakratu was king of the gods,

sanskrit: ijyamāneṣu deveṣu cāturvarṇye vyavasthite samṛdhyamāne trailokye prītiyukte svayaṃbhuvi
english: when the gods were being worshipped with sacrifice and the four orders were established, when the triple world was flourishing and the Self-existent was content,

sanskrit: rudrair vasubhir ādityair aśvibhyām api carṣibhiḥ gandharvair bhujagendraiś ca siddhaiś cānyair vṛtaḥ prabhuḥ
english: the lord, attended by the Rudras, the Vasus, the Ādityas, and by the two Aśvins and the seers, by the Gandharvas and the lords of serpents and the Siddhas and others,

sanskrit: caturdantaṃ sudāntaṃ ca vāraṇendraṃ śriyā vṛtam āruhyairāvataṃ śakras trailokyam anusaṃyayau
english: mounting Airāvata, the four-tusked and well-tamed lord of elephants, decked with splendor, Śakra ranged throughout the triple world.

sanskrit: sa kadā cit samudrānte kasmiṃś cid girigahvare baliṃ vairocaniṃ vajrī dadarśopasasarpa ca
english: Once, by the shore of the ocean, in a certain mountain cavern, the wielder of the thunderbolt beheld Bali the son of Virocana, and drew near to him.

sanskrit: tam airāvatamūrdhasthaṃ prekṣya devagaṇair vṛtam surendram indraṃ daityendro na śuśoca na vivyathe
english: Beholding him, Indra the lord of the gods, seated on Airāvata's brow and surrounded by the hosts of heaven, the lord of the Daityas neither grieved nor trembled.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tam avikārasthaṃ tiṣṭhantaṃ nirbhayaṃ balim adhirūḍho dvipaśreṣṭham ity uvāca śatakratuḥ
english: Seeing Bali standing unmoved and unafraid, Śatakratu, mounted upon the best of elephants, spoke thus:

sanskrit: daitya na vyathase śauryād atha vā vṛddhasevayā tapasā bhāvitatvād vā sarvathaitat suduṣkaram
english: O Daitya, you do not tremble—whether from valor, or from service to your elders, or from being purified by austerity; in any case this is most hard to do.

sanskrit: śatrubhir vaśam ānīto hīnaḥ sthānād anuttamāt vairocane kim āśritya śocitavye na śocasi
english: Brought into the power of your foes, fallen from a station unsurpassed—O son of Virocana, upon what do you rely that, when there is cause for grief, you do not grieve?

sanskrit: śraiṣṭhyaṃ prāpya svajātīnāṃ bhuktvā bhogān anuttamān hṛtasvabalarājyas tvaṃ brūhi kasmān na śocasi
english: Having gained supremacy over your own kind and enjoyed pleasures unsurpassed, now robbed of your own host and kingdom—tell me, why do you not grieve?

sanskrit: īśvaro hi purā bhūtvā pitṛpaitāmahe pade tat tvam adya hṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā sapatnaiḥ kiṃ na śocasi
english: For having once been lord in the seat of your fathers and forefathers, why do you not grieve to see it today carried off by your rivals?

sanskrit: baddhaś ca vāruṇaiḥ pāśair vajreṇa ca samāhataḥ hṛtadāro hṛtadhano brūhi kasmān na śocasi
english: Bound by Varuṇa's fetters and smitten by the thunderbolt, your wife taken, your wealth taken—tell me, why do you not grieve?

sanskrit: bhraṣṭaśrīr vibhavabhraṣṭo yan na śocasi duṣkaram trailokyarājyanāśe hi ko 'nyo jīvitum utsahet
english: That you do not grieve, fallen from fortune and stripped of majesty, is hard indeed; for at the loss of the kingdom of the three worlds, who else would have the heart to live?

sanskrit: etac cānyac ca paruṣaṃ bruvantaṃ paribhūya tam śrutvā sukham asaṃbhrānto balir vairocano 'bravīt
english: Having heard him speak these words and other harsh ones besides, Bali the son of Virocana, contemning him, calmly and unflustered replied:

sanskrit: nigṛhīte mayi bhṛśaṃ śakra kiṃ katthitena te vajram udyamya tiṣṭhantaṃ paśyāmi tvāṃ puraṃdara
english: When I am thus utterly subdued, O Śakra, what use is this boasting of yours? I see you standing with the thunderbolt upraised, O Purandara.

sanskrit: aśaktaḥ pūrvam āsīs tvaṃ kathaṃ cic chaktatāṃ gataḥ kas tvad anya imā vācaḥ sukrūrā vaktum arhati
english: Formerly you were powerless; somehow you have come into power. Who other than you would deign to utter these most cruel words?

sanskrit: yas tu śatror vaśasthasya śakto 'pi kurute dayām hastaprāptasya vīrasya taṃ caiva puruṣaṃ viduḥ
english: But he who, though able, shows mercy to a foe in his power, to a hero fallen into his very hands—him they account a true man.

sanskrit: aniścayo hi yuddheṣu dvayor vivadamānayoḥ ekaḥ prāpnoti vijayam ekaś caiva parābhavam
english: For in battles between two contending parties there is no certainty: one attains victory, and one attains defeat.

sanskrit: mā ca te bhūt svabhāvo 'yaṃ mayā daivatapuṃgava īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vikrameṇa jito balāt
english: And let this not be your settled persuasion, O bull among the gods—that the lord of all beings was conquered by your valor through main strength.

sanskrit: naitad asmatkṛtaṃ śakra naitac chakra tvayā kṛtam yat tvam evaṃgato vajrin yad vāpy evaṃgatā vayam
english: This was not done by us, O Śakra, nor was this done by you, O Śakra—that you have come to such a state, O wielder of the thunderbolt, or that we have come to such a state.

sanskrit: aham āsaṃ yathādya tvaṃ bhavitā tvaṃ yathā vayam māvamaṃsthā mayā karma duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ity uta
english: What you are today, that I once was; and what we now are, that you shall become. Do not despise me, thinking, 'It is by some evil deed of his own doing.'

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhe hi puruṣaḥ paryāyeṇādhigacchati paryāyeṇāsi śakratvaṃ prāptaḥ śakra na karmaṇā
english: For a man comes upon pleasure and pain by turns; by the turning of fate you have attained the lordship of Śakra, O Śakra, and not by your own deed.

sanskrit: kālaḥ kāle nayati māṃ tvāṃ ca kālo nayaty ayam tenāhaṃ tvaṃ yathā nādya tvaṃ cāpi na yathā vayam
english: Time leads me on in its time, and this same Time leads you on as well; therefore I am not now as you are, nor are you as we are.

sanskrit: na mātṛpitṛśuśrūṣā na ca daivatapūjanam nānyo guṇasamācāraḥ puruṣasya sukhāvahaḥ
english: Neither dutiful service to mother and father, nor worship of the gods, nor any other practice of virtue, brings happiness to a man on its own.

sanskrit: na vidyā na tapo dānaṃ na mitrāṇi na bāndhavāḥ śaknuvanti paritrātuṃ naraṃ kālena pīḍitam
english: Not learning, not austerity, not giving, not friends, not kinsmen are able to rescue a man oppressed by Time.

sanskrit: nāgāminam anarthaṃ hi pratighātaśatair api śaknuvanti prativyoḍhum ṛte buddhibalān narāḥ
english: For the misfortune that is to come, men cannot ward off even with a hundred counterstrokes, save by the strength of their understanding.

sanskrit: paryāyair hanyamānānāṃ paritrātā na vidyate idaṃ tu duḥkhaṃ yac chakra kartāham iti manyate
english: For those struck down by the turns of fate there is found no deliverer; but this is the suffering, O Śakra—that one thinks, 'I am the doer.'

sanskrit: yadi kartā bhavet kartā na kriyeta kadā cana yasmāt tu kriyate kartā tasmāt kartāpy anīśvaraḥ
english: If the doer were truly the doer, he would never himself be acted upon; but since the doer too is acted upon, therefore even the doer is not sovereign.

sanskrit: kālena tvāham ajayaṃ kālenāhaṃ jitas tvayā gantā gatimatāṃ kālaḥ kālaḥ kalayati prajāḥ
english: By Time I once conquered you, and by Time I have been conquered by you; Time is the mover of all that moves, Time impels all creatures onward.

sanskrit: indra prākṛtayā buddhyā pralapan nāvabudhyase ke cit tvāṃ bahu manyante śraiṣṭhyaṃ prāptaṃ svakarmaṇā
english: O Indra, prattling with your common understanding, you do not comprehend; some hold you in high esteem, deeming you to have won supremacy by your own deed.

sanskrit: katham asmadvidho nāma jānaṃl lokapravṛttayaḥ kālenābhyāhataḥ śocen muhyed vāpy arthasaṃbhrame
english: How should one such as I, who knows the workings of the world, grieve when struck down by Time, or be bewildered amid the upheaval of his fortunes?
